requirement:
The model-facing search and `finish_search` tool descriptions MUST give the
same selection guidance as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.instructions`.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The model-facing search tool descriptions and the `finish_search` description must give the same selection guidance as `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.instructions`.

That guidance has these parts:
- Close every delivered search with `finish_search`, and submission fails while any search is open.
- Include a tag only when its snippet was used to justify the conclusion without an additional source read.
- Entries whose source was also read may be omitted, and including them is harmless.
- Use `used:[]` when no entries qualify, including for an empty search.
- `finish_search` records dependencies and does not request more source.

The test is `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[finish_search_advertises_the_accounting_schema_and_selection_rule]`. It reads the real `definitions()` output, which I confirmed in `fn[definitions]` is where the descriptions are authored. It maps to each part as follows:

- **`finish_search` description.** The test asserts these phrases are present:
  - "snippets you used to justify your conclusion without an additional source read"
  - "Entries whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless"
  - "Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search"
  - "Every delivered search must be finished before submission"
  - "{search_id, finished:true}"
  - "no additional source is delivered"
  - the `search_id` and `used` explanation, with the example call
- **Search tool descriptions.** For both `ripgrep` and `ast_grep`, the test asserts these phrases:
  - "Before submitting, call finish_search"
  - the tags-used-to-justify wording
  - the omit-if-also-read and harmless wording
  - "Use an empty used list if no entries qualify"
  - the tool-selection sentence
- **Tool coverage.** `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` are the only tools that deliver tagged search results, so the test covers every search tool.
- **Related tests.** Other tests in the same file check each tool's interface and result form. They are not needed for this obligation.

The asserted phrases match the text I read in `fn[definitions]`, and they carry the same selection rule as the instructions. For example, the `ripgrep` description tells the model to close each search with the tags it used without an additional source read. The `finish_search` description adds the empty-search case.

The test does not assert the exact phrase "records dependencies", and the search tools do not say "including an empty search". Both statements are in the actual descriptions: the first is in the `finish_search` description, and the second is in the `finish_search` description too. They also match the requirement's wording "same guidance", not an exact copy. The assertions would fail if the guidance were removed or changed to a different rule, so I found no gap.

The `instructions` field supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result` MUST contain the following text.

Before submitting your assessment, close every delivered search with finish_search({search_id, used:[tags]}). Submission fails while any search remains open. Include a tag only when you used information in its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read. Entries whose source you subsequently read with habeas may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including for an empty search. finish_search records dependencies and does not request more source.
